 Roku Adds 8 New Free Live Channels on Roku TVs & Roku Players
 By
 Luke Bouma 
 on
 November 17, 2026 
 in 
 All News , News , Roku 
 Roku has expanded the free live television offerings available on Roku TVs and Roku streaming players by adding eight new channels to T he Roku Channel guide . The new streams join the platform’s existing collection of more than 500 ad-supported linear channels and require no additional subscription or fee beyond owning a compatible Roku device. Viewers can locate the additions by opening The Roku Channel, navigating to the Live TV section, and either scrolling the guide or searching by channel number or name.
 Channel 814 carries Swerve Sports Talk, a discussion-oriented feed focused on sports conversation and analysis. It draws from the broader Swerve Sports ecosystem, which specializes in women’s athletics including basketball, volleyball, soccer, softball, and other competitions, often featuring highlights, commentary, and related programming aimed at fans seeking ongoing coverage without a paid sports package.
 Channel 2417 is 365 BLK (FAST), a continuous entertainment stream centered on African American movies, series, and cultural programming. The channel typically cycles through feature films, classic television episodes, and related content designed for round-the-clock viewing, fitting into the growing lineup of targeted free linear options on the platform.
 Channel 2516 presents Roku Case of the Week, a specialized feed that highlights individual true-crime or investigative stories on a rotating basis. Programming centers on case examinations, reconstructions, and related material, providing a dedicated linear destination for viewers who prefer episodic deep dives into real-life investigations.
 Channel 2688 features Snapped, the long-running true-crime series that examines cases involving women accused of murder. Episodes typically reconstruct events through interviews, evidence reviews, and narrative accounts, and the new linear channel allows continuous access to the catalog without switching between on-demand libraries.
 Channel 4523 is Botherd, a lighter or talk-oriented stream that appears oriented toward conversational or comedy-tinged content. The addition broadens the platform’s mix of discussion formats alongside more traditional entertainment and news linear channels.
 Channel 5120 is 1230! Spanish, a Spanish-language option that expands the guide’s offerings for bilingual and Spanish-preferring households. Content focuses on programming tailored to those audiences, consistent with Roku’s ongoing efforts to increase non-English linear choices.
 Channel 5121 carries Ideas en 5 Minutos, a Spanish-language lifestyle and how-to channel built around short visual tutorials. Programming includes quick crafts, DIY projects, home tips, and practical life hacks aimed at families and viewers looking for concise instructional segments that can play in the background or for active watching.
 Channel 5122 is Zona, another Spanish-language addition that further diversifies the free guide with culturally relevant entertainment, talk, or regional programming. Together with the other Spanish channels in the update, it strengthens options for Hispanic viewers who rely on free streaming rather than traditional cable packages.
 All eight channels operate under The Roku Channel’s standard free, ad-supported model. Availability can vary slightly by region and device software version, and channel numbers occasionally shift as the guide is reorganized. For households that have cut the cord or never subscribed to traditional pay TV, the expansion supplies additional sports talk, true-crime loops, Black-focused entertainment, lifestyle tutorials, and Spanish-language streams at no extra cost. Users simply power on a Roku TV or player, open The Roku Channel, and enter the Live TV guide to begin watching immediately. The update continues Roku’s pattern of regularly enlarging its free linear lineup to keep the platform competitive with other ad-supported streaming services.
